utility.notes: The City of Bend's own franchise ordinance (No. NS-2346) states directly: 'PacifiCorp dba Pacific Power (Pacific Power) provides electric power distribution utility services in a portion of the City of Bend.' A separate City electrification-policy study estimated the City's electric utility mix as weighted approximately 85% Pacific Power and 15% Central Electric Cooperative (CEC) — Bend is a genuine two-utility city, similar in structure to Phoenix (APS/SRP) and Mesa (municipal/SRP). This record is scoped to the Pacific Power-served majority only; Central Electric Cooperative customers within Bend are NOT covered by this record and would need independent verification of CEC's own interconnection process.

value.name: Oregon Solar + Storage Rebate Program (OSSRP) — Energy Storage System
value.description: Statewide Oregon rebate for residential energy storage systems paired with a solar electric system: $300 per kWh of installed storage capacity, up to 60% of net system cost or $2,500 (whichever is less) for low/moderate-income homeowners, or up to 40% of net cost or $2,500 for other homeowners. Rebates are issued to ODOE-approved contractors, who pass savings to the customer at time of installation. As of this record's verification date (June 2026 update on ODOE's own page), the program is NOT currently accepting new rebate reservation applications — the $1.1 million reopened on June 15, 2026 was fully reserved almost immediately. This is a genuine, temporary funding-exhaustion pause, not a program termination.
value.eligibility: Must be installed on Oregon real property by an ODOE-approved contractor; storage must be paired at time of installation with a previously purchased/installed (or concurrently purchased) solar electric system; reservation application required before construction begins.

value.name: Oregon Solar + Storage Rebate Program (OSSRP) — Solar Electric System
value.description: Statewide Oregon rebate for residential solar electric systems: low/moderate-income homeowners receive $1.80/watt(DC), up to 60% of net cost or $5,000 (whichever is less); homeowners not low/moderate-income but eligible for a utility incentive receive $0.20/watt(DC) up to 40% of net cost or $5,000; homeowners not eligible for a utility incentive receive $0.50/watt(DC) up to 40% of net cost or $5,000. Rebates are issued to ODOE-approved contractors, who pass savings to the customer directly. As of this record's verification date (June 2026 update on ODOE's own page), the program is NOT currently accepting new rebate reservation applications — the $1.1 million reopened on June 15, 2026 was fully reserved almost immediately. This is a genuine, temporary funding-exhaustion pause, not a program termination.
value.eligibility: Must be installed on Oregon real property by an ODOE-approved contractor; reservation application required before construction begins; must meet minimum Total Solar Resource Fraction and other technical criteria.
